title: Sum
statement: Given an integer n followed by n space-separated integers, compute and print the sum of all n elements exactly once. The current implementation skips one element because of an incorrect loop boundary. Fix the iteration so every valid index from 0 to n-1 is included, and ensure the output is a single integer with no extra text.

title: Condition Check
statement: You are given n integers and must print how many of them are even. The buggy code checks the opposite parity and therefore counts odd values instead. Correct the condition so only values divisible by 2 are counted. Output a single integer representing the total even count.

title: Variable
statement: Read n integers and print the maximum element. The current code uses a maximum accumulator before assigning it a valid initial value, which can cause undefined behavior. Initialize the maximum correctly (for example from the first element) and then process all elements safely. Output only the maximum integer.

title: Array Access
statement: You are given n and then n integers. Print the last element of the array. The buggy program reads one extra element using an invalid index, causing out-of-bounds access. Fix the input loop to read exactly n values and keep array accesses within [0, n-1]. Output only the last value.

title: Loop Bound
statement: Given an integer n, count how many numbers are in the sequence from 1 to n inclusive and print that count. The current loop excludes one endpoint due to a wrong bound. Correct the loop so the program reports exactly n when n is non-negative. Print a single integer.

title: Safe Division
statement: Read two integers a and b and print integer division a/b. However, when b is zero, division must be treated as invalid and the output must be 0 instead of crashing. Fix the runtime error by adding a safe check before division. Output only one integer.

title: Return Value
statement: Implement factorial(n) recursively and print n!. The base case is incorrect in the buggy version, which returns 0 for n = 0 and breaks the full recursion chain. Fix the return value for the base case so factorial works for 0 and all positive inputs. Output only the factorial value.

title: String Reverse
statement: Given a string s without spaces, print its reversed form. The buggy code calls reverse with an empty range, so the string remains unchanged. Correct the range so all characters are reversed from beginning to end. Output only the reversed string.

title: Sorting
statement: Read n integers, sort them in non-decreasing order, and print the sorted sequence separated by spaces. The current call to sort uses an invalid end iterator, so sorting does not process the full array. Fix the sort range to include every element. Preserve numeric order and output formatting.

title: Min Value
statement: Given n integers, print the minimum value in the array. The buggy implementation initializes the minimum with 0, which is incorrect for all-positive inputs and can mask real answers. Initialize the tracker properly (for example first element) and evaluate all numbers. Output one integer.

title: Fibonacci
statement: Given n, print the nth Fibonacci number using the standard definition F(0)=0 and F(1)=1. The buggy base case returns 1 for both 0 and 1, shifting all results. Correct the recursive logic so each n maps to the expected Fibonacci value. Output only the computed number.

title: Prefix Sum
statement: Read an array of n integers and transform it into prefix sums where each element i becomes sum of elements from 0 to i. Print the transformed array in order with spaces. Ensure accumulation is performed left to right for all valid indices. Output must match exact prefix totals.

title: Comparator
statement: Given n integers, sort and print them in non-increasing (descending) order. The buggy implementation sorts in ascending order because it uses the default comparator. Apply the correct comparator so larger numbers appear first. Print values separated by spaces.

title: Binary Search
statement: Given a sorted array and a target x, print YES if x exists in the array, otherwise print NO. The binary search loop and boundary updates are flawed, which can miss valid answers near the end of the search range. Fix conditions so all candidate positions are checked safely. Output exactly YES or NO.

title: GCD
statement: Read two integers a and b and print their greatest common divisor using Euclid's algorithm. The buggy base case returns b when b becomes zero, which is incorrect and causes wrong answers. Fix the termination condition so recursion returns the correct divisor. Output one integer.
